ranking.note: Raised to P1: release-binary verification accepting revoked/expired keys is a security flaw in tooling operators depend on, responsibly disclosed; worst consequence in this category.
Raised to P2 to match #36105: both are outright failures of the bitcoin wrapper on supported platforms/distros, not mere inconvenience.
Raised to P2: a tool that touches transactions silently emits bare scripts instead of P2SH/P2WSH and exits 0, a correctness/fund-safety consequence the category ranks just after operator tooling.

Raised to P3: the card describes options after positional arguments being silently swallowed (including -rpcwallet misrouting) across cli/wallet/tx, the same class of silent misparse as #36368, not an incidental cleanup.
Moved up: seed generation is explicitly the first-priority tool in this category and the bug aborts a release-time run.
Moved down relative to its own score: a new developer/researcher convenience ranks below tool bugs that break operator workflows.
Moved down: self-described working prototype for a tracking issue, real value but clearly deferrable against tool breakages.
Moved down: groundwork whose payoff is a future PR (#19461); no user-visible change yet beyond the scaffold.
Moved down: internal developer dependency checker with no user-facing effect, and unresolved design-doc concerns; lowest-value P3 here.
Lowered to P4: draft the author himself prefers to abandon in favour of manual rewrites, and the check introduced a witness-dropping bug; speculative within tools.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36190 only tests behaviour introduced by #36105; review #36105 first, #36190 is near-meaningless without it.

#36105 and #36106 both fix the bitcoin wrapper and touch its process/path handling; review #36105 first (execution model) then #36106 (install paths) to avoid conflicting assumptions about how children are located and launched.

#35831 (GNU-style option parsing in ArgsManager) and #36368 (bitcoin-tx rejecting over-separated arguments) both attack silently misparsed command-line input; they are not duplicates but overlap in intent — decide the general argsman approach in #35831 before locking in the tool-specific check in #36368.
#35903 may be redundant: a reviewer asked whether #35958 already makes the non-printable msgtype path unreachable; confirm before spending review time.
#35994 duplicates work the author says should instead be done as manual declarative rewrites; treat as a candidate for closing rather than review.
result.notes: Band spread is intentional: one security-grade tooling fix (P1), three tool-breakage/correctness fixes (P2), a long tail of genuine but deferrable contrib and developer-tool improvements (P3), and two marginal items (P4). Several P3 positions differ noticeably from the solo scores because the category ranks operator-facing tools (seeds, wrapper, verification) above developer convenience regardless of polish or activity.
